name: Nebushazban
overview: Nebushazban was a male official known as the Rab-saris, a chief court officer or palace official, as mentioned in Jeremiah 39:13. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal details. His role as Rab-saris indicates a position of significant authority within the Babylonian administration.
namesAndTitles: The name Nebushazban means "Nebo [Nabu] save me!" reflecting a theophoric element invoking the Babylonian deity Nabu. The title Rab-saris translates to chief court official, palace officer, or eunuch, highlighting his high-ranking position in the royal court. Both the name and title are noted in Jeremiah 39:13.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Nebushazban beyond his designation as the Rab-saris. There are no additional relational details provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Nebushazban's significance lies in his role as a chief official during the Babylonian period, specifically referenced in Jeremiah 39:13. His position as Rab-saris places him among the key figures involved in the administration and events surrounding Jerusalem's fall, illustrating the political and military structure of Babylon at that time. Though details are brief, his mention contributes to the historical and prophetic narrative concerning God's judgment on Judah.
